criteria.name: Mission concept and rationale — What will it do, who are the users, why is it needed?
criteria.reasoning: The rationale and users (marine scientists) are clearly identified, benefiting the Great Barrier Reef. However, formal engineering requirements (e.g., revisit rate, spectral bands, spatial resolution) are absent.

evidence.quote: A near-real-time relay to monitoring stations on the ground would allow marine and conservation scientists to more accurately predict and react to coral bleaching events.

criteria.name: Project plan — How you plan to complete the assignment, including either a Gantt chart or a timetable and information sources you plan to use
criteria.reasoning: A Gantt chart and task breakdowns are provided, linking back to the mission stages. However, contingencies, risk mitigation, and project variation planning are missing.

evidence.quote: Project work will be divided into weeks via a Gantt Chart. Detailed task descriptions can be found on the next page.

criteria.name: Preliminary progress — Technical content and evidence of sufficient work done to date
criteria.reasoning: There is virtually no actual preliminary technical output (no preliminary orbit calculations, constellation analysis, or STK outputs), only a statement that tutorials were completed.

evidence.quote: Furthermore, in my progress, I have read the brief of Asner’s monitoring system in Hawaii, researched into how coral bleaching occurs and its severity, and also completed STK tutorials 1, 2, 3 & 4.

criteria.name: Report presentation
criteria.reasoning: The report has a neat layout and readable prose, but referencing consists entirely of bare URLs rather than formal bibliographic citations.

technical_issues.issue: Leaving an Earth-observation satellite 'where it is' at end-of-life violates standard space debris mitigation guidelines (e.g. 25-year de-orbit rule in LEO).

overall: Good conceptual foundation and a clear Gantt chart, but technical progress is lacking: no engineering analysis, orbit calculations, or STK figures are included.

feedback.summary: You have established a solid mission rationale targeting Great Barrier Reef conservation, supported by a structured schedule and clean layout. However, your submission currently lacks quantitative engineering analysis, formal functional requirements, and space debris mitigation planning. To advance to higher bands, you must produce preliminary technical results such as orbit simulations and calculations, define explicit mission performance requirements, incorporate risk management into your project plan, and replace bare URLs with formal academic citations.
next_steps: Conduct preliminary orbital and payload technical analysis (e.g., using STK to evaluate coverage and revisit rates) and include annotated data or figures.

Formulate specific engineering requirements (e.g., spatial resolution, spectral bands, revisit frequency) linked to the needs of marine scientists, and update your end-of-life disposal plan to comply with LEO space debris mitigation standards.
Upgrade the 'Useful Links' section into a formal referencing style (e.g., IEEE or Harvard) with matching in-text citations, and add contingency planning to your project schedule.

criteria.C1: You clearly identified marine scientists as end users in 'Mission Concept & Rationale'. To achieve Accomplished, translate this concept into formal engineering requirements—such as explicit revisit rates, spectral bands, and spatial resolution—supported by literature citations.
criteria.C2: Your Gantt chart and task breakdown in 'Project Plan & Preliminary Progress' lay out a workable schedule. To reach Accomplished, build a more robust plan by incorporating contingency provisions, risk mitigation, and planned responses to project variations.
criteria.C3: While completing STK tutorials shows preparation, listing completed tutorials does not demonstrate technical progress. To reach Adequate or Accomplished, you must include actual engineering outputs, such as preliminary orbit trade-offs, coverage calculations, or STK visualisations with accompanying interpretation.
criteria.C4: Your report is neat, readable, and structured with clear sections. To reach Accomplished, format the bare URLs in 'Useful Links' into complete, consistent bibliographic citations (e.g., author, year, title) and ensure every source is correctly cited in-text.
